verdict.summary: You create a Notion public connection in the Developer portal and can use OAuth right away. Notion's docs say a public connection can be used without a Marketplace listing. Review only applies if you want a Marketplace listing, which needs a Notion security review plus a listing review. One catch: the portal only fills in the Authorization URL field after you submit for review. You can still build the authorize URL yourself from your client ID.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 20-40 min for a working OAuth app. Add 1-3 hours if you also prepare a Marketplace listing.
verdict.approval_wait: None for OAuth use. For an optional Marketplace listing, Notion says to expect a reply in 5-10 business days. No timeline is published for the security review.

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion account through your own client ID/secret and Composio callback.
limits: The portal leaves the Authorization URL field empty until you submit for review. Build the authorize URL yourself (or let Composio build it) from client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.
Rate limit per connection: 180 requests/min, or 600/min on Business and Enterprise plans. A separate limit applies per workspace.

gates.name: Unlisted public connection (shared with specific users)
gates.unlocks: Other users in any workspace (or only selected workspaces, depending on installation scope) can authorize through the OAuth flow. Each user gets their own token.
limits: Notion's docs list no install cap or user cap for unlisted or unreviewed public connections.
Each user has to complete the auth flow themselves. There is no automatic workspace-wide install.
If you chose 'Selected workspaces only' at creation, you can't change it later, and the connection can never be listed on the Marketplace.
gates.time_to_reach: Same as Gate 1. No extra step is documented.

gates.name: Marketplace listing (optional)
gates.unlocks: People can find your connection on the Notion Marketplace. The OAuth flow already works for anyone without a listing.
limits: Requires a Notion security review and a review of every listing submission. Possible rejection reasons include brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, and failing baseline connection criteria.
gates.time_to_reach: 5-10 business days for a listing reply, plus a security review with no published timeline

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own connection
steps.detail: Composio's managed Notion OAuth is enough for testing. Register your own public connection when you want your own branding and your own client ID/secret. A personal access token does not replace this: it only covers your own scripts and has no OAuth flow or page picker.

steps.title: Open Public connections in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in at app.notion.com/developers/connections. In the sidebar, go to the Build section, select Public connections, then click Create new connection.

steps.title: Enter name, development workspace and installation scope
steps.detail: Enter a connection name and pick your development workspace. For installation scope, choose 'Any workspace' unless you are sure you will never want a Marketplace listing.
gotchas: You can't change installation scope after creation. A connection set to 'Selected workspaces only' can't be listed on the Marketplace, so you would have to build a new one.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: Under OAuth configuration, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. If you register more than one redirect URI, the token exchange must send the same redirect_uri that was used in the authorize request.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The callback must match exactly what your Composio project uses (for example, a v1 auth-apps URL and a v3 callback are different URLs).

steps.title: Choose minimal capabilities
steps.detail: Map your agent's tools to the capability groups it actually needs: content (read, update, insert), comments (read, insert) and user info (none, without emails, with emails). Then tick only those boxes. Notion says workspace admins are more likely to install a connection that asks for fewer capabilities.
gotchas: If you change capabilities after users have authorized, they all have to re-authenticate. Settle the set before you invite anyone.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth client ID and secret
steps.detail: After you create the connection, open its Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret somewhere safe.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the notion toolkit and enter your client ID and secret. Leave scopes empty, because Notion controls access through capabilities, not scope strings. The authorize request uses client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, approve it in Notion's page picker, and check that the token exchange returns an access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace fields. Then make one API call to confirm access works.
gotchas: The portal's Authorization URL field stays blank until you submit for review. Use the authorize URL that Composio builds instead.
With a fake client ID, the authorize endpoint showed a JavaScript-only install page instead of an OAuth error. Check the client ID carefully if the page looks broken.

steps.title: Check that refresh-token rotation is stored
steps.detail: Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Whatever stores the tokens has to save the new refresh token every time. Ignore older community posts that say Notion has no refresh tokens.

steps.title: Share the connection with other users
steps.detail: Send other users through your app's Composio connect flow. Each user must authorize individually and gets their own token. No review is needed for this.

steps.title: Optional: draft the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Draft the listing name, description, category and tags, listing images and logo, and link the public connection. Check the draft against Notion's Connection Gallery Best Practices guide.

steps.title: Optional: save and submit the listing
steps.detail: In the Listings > Connections page, save the draft and submit it. Notion's security review of the public connection is required before it can be listed.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's review
steps.detail: Follow the status on the listing dashboard. Notion says to expect an email within 5-10 business days. If rejected, the email gives the reason; fix it and resubmit.

requirements.item: Notion account with a development workspace
requirements.detail: You pick a development workspace when you create the public connection.

requirements.item: Redirect URI registered on the connection
requirements.detail: Must exactly match the Composio callback URL used in the authorize and token requests.
Pick content, comment and user-info capabilities when you create the connection.
Needed for a Marketplace listing. You can't change it after creation.
Needed before listing. Notion doesn't publish a timeline or checklist.
Name, description, category, tags, listing images, logo, and the linked public connection.

scopes.effect: The basic read capability. Notion has no scope strings; you tick this in the connection's capabilities.
Lets the connection change or add content. Notion publishes no sensitivity tiers. Requesting fewer capabilities makes admins more likely to install.
Comment access. Only request it if your agent uses comment tools.
The most sensitive user-level option. It controls listing all users and retrieving a user with emails. Changing it later forces everyone to re-authenticate.

blockers.symptom: The Authorization URL field in the Developer portal is empty.
blockers.cause: Notion fills in this field only after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Build the authorize URL from client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user, or let Composio build it.

blockers.symptom: You can't list the connection on the Marketplace.
blockers.cause: Installation scope was set to 'Selected workspaces only', and it can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace'.

blockers.symptom: Users are asked to authorize again after you edit the connection.
blockers.cause: Capabilities changed after users had authorized.
blockers.fix: Settle capabilities before sharing the connection, and warn users before any change.

blockers.symptom: Teammates in the same workspace can't use your agent.
blockers.cause: Public connections are per user, so each user has to complete the auth flow.
blockers.fix: Have each user connect through the Composio flow themselves.

blockers.cause: Per-connection limit (180/min, or 600/min on Business and Enterprise) or the shared per-workspace limit.
blockers.fix: Back off using Retry-After and spread requests out.

blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or failing baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Fix the reason given in the email and resubmit.

composio.note: Composio offers managed OAuth2 for Notion (authorize URL https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize, token URL https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token) with an empty scope list, because Notion sets access through capabilities and the page picker. Start on managed auth to test. Switch to your own public connection when you want your own branding, your own client ID/secret, or your own install flow. If you use your own connection, register the exact Composio callback URL from your auth config as the redirect URI. A Marketplace listing is separate and optional.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created in the Developer portal under the Build section, using Public connections and Create new connection; the portal is at app.notion.com.
evidence.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing requires a draft with name and description, category and tags, listing images and logo, and the associated public connection, saved then submitted from the Listings > Connections page.
evidence.quote: Listing name and description; Category and tags; Listing images and logo

evidence.claim: Notion's docs for the listing point to a separate connection gallery best practices guide for review tips; the page itself does not list privacy policy, domain verification, or demo video requirements.
evidence.quote: Notion Connection Gallery Best Practices

evidence.claim: Notion does not use OAuth scope strings; access is set by capabilities, which are content (read, update, insert), comment (read, insert), and user (none, without emails, with emails) groups.
evidence.quote: Content capabilities; Comment capabilities; User capabilities

evidence.claim: The user-information capability with email addresses is the most sensitive user-level option; it controls access to listing all users and retrieving a user.
evidence.quote: User information with email addresses

evidence.claim: Notion advises requesting the fewest capabilities; the fewer requested, the more likely a workspace admin will install the connection.
evidence.quote: The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection.

evidence.claim: Changing capabilities after users have authorized forces those users to re-authenticate.
evidence.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs are entered under OAuth configuration at creation; the token exchange must use the same redirect_uri when more than one is registered or when it was passed in the authorize URL.
evidence.quote: The redirect_uri is a required field in the request body for this endpoint if

evidence.claim: The authorize request takes client_id, redirect_uri, response_type set to code, owner set to user, and an optional state.
evidence.quote: owner | Always use user.

evidence.claim: The token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret, and returns an access token, a refresh token, a bot ID, owner, and workspace fields.
evidence.quote: Notion responds to the request with an access_token, refresh_token, and additional information.

evidence.claim: Refreshing uses grant_type refresh_token and returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so the refresh token has to be stored again each time.
evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: Creation requires a connection name, a development workspace, redirect URI(s), an installation scope, and the capabilities the connection needs.
evidence.quote: Connection name and development workspace; Redirect URI(s) for the OAuth flow; Installation scope

evidence.claim: A community guide claims the Notion access token never expires and that there is no refresh token. This conflicts with Notion's current official auth page, which documents refresh tokens, so the official page should be treated as current.
evidence.quote: There is no refresh token mechanism; revocation requires the full OAuth flow again.

evidence.claim: Public connections are not tied to one workspace; each user who authorizes gets their own token, and each user must complete the auth flow individually, so a workspace-wide install is not automatic.
evidence.quote: each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.

evidence.claim: Probing the authorize endpoint with a fake client ID and the Composio callback as redirect_uri did not produce an OAuth error parameter; it redirected to app.notion.com/install-integration and rendered a JavaScript-only page. The endpoint is live; an invalid client is not rejected server-side in this probe.
evidence.quote: Notion JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: Rate limits: each connection gets a per-minute budget: 180 requests per minute on all plans except Business and Enterprise, which get 600 per minute; a separate per-workspace limit is shared across all connections in a workspace.
evidence.quote: Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second)

evidence.claim: Notion's request-limit page does not mention any install cap or user cap for unreviewed or unlisted public connections, nor any approval-based rate increase.
evidence.quote: Per-connection limit | Per-workspace limit

evidence.claim: Notion's changelog says the per-connection limit moved to a fixed 60-second window on September 9, 2026, with a 60-second Retry-After cap.
evidence.quote: The per-connection rate limit is now enforced over a fixed 60-second window

evidence.claim: After creation, the OAuth client ID and client secret are read from the Configuration tab of the connection.
evidence.quote: visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret.

evidence.claim: A third-party tutorial says the Notion public integration needs a company name and website under Organization Information, plus an optional logo; official Notion pages describe listing images and logo fields.
evidence.quote: Enter your company name and website in the Organization Information section.

evidence.claim: Notion's Marketplace is a separate listing in the Listings > Connections dashboard; the listing is optional and does not affect whether the OAuth flow works for users.
evidence.quote: Listing on the Marketplace is optional and helps your connection reach a wider audience

evidence.claim: A personal access token route exists for a single user's own scripts and trusted tools; it has no OAuth flow and no page picker, so it does not help other users install the app.
evidence.quote: There is no OAuth flow and no page picker.

evidence.claim: The authorization URL field on a new public connection stays empty until the connection has been submitted for review, so the install link is not available before submission.
evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

evidence.claim: Installation scope is chosen at creation and can't be changed later: Any workspace is Marketplace-eligible, while Selected workspaces only is not. Choosing Selected workspaces only means building a new connection if a Marketplace listing is wanted later.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: Public connections must pass a Notion security review before they can be listed on the Marketplace, but a connection can be created and used without listing it.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listings are reviewed by the Notion team on every submission; the listing dashboard tracks status, and rejections come with an email explaining the reason.
evidence.quote: The Notion team reviews every listing submission.

evidence.claim: Notion's FAQ says to expect a reply on a Marketplace submission within 5-10 business days; this is stated for the listing, and no separate timeline for the security review is published.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Rejections can be for brand or trademark problems, quality concerns, or failing the baseline connection criteria; Notion invites a fix and resubmission.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns

open_questions: Does an authorize URL you build yourself work for other users before the connection is submitted for review, given that the portal's Authorization URL field stays empty until submission?
No install or user cap for unreviewed public connections is documented. Notion may still have one that isn't published.
Notion's security review has no published timeline or checklist. The 5-10 business day figure is for the Marketplace listing reply.
